question: What high-visibility apparel is generally required for workers within a temporary traffic control zone?
model_answer: Direct Answer: All workers within the right-of-way who are within a TTC zone—during both daytime and nighttime activity—must wear high-visibility safety apparel meeting ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 Performance Class 2 or 3 requirements, with the appropriate class selected by an employer-designated safety person. This requirement extends to uniformed law enforcement directing traffic and, with limited exceptions, to firefighters and other emergency responders; certain responders may instead wear ANSI/ISEA 207-2006 public safety vests. Standards (mandatory): - "For daytime and nighttime activity, all workers, including emergency responders, within the right-of-way who are within the TTC zone shall wear high-visibility safety apparel that meets the Performance Class 2 or 3 requirements of the ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 publication entitled 'American National Standard for High-Visibility Safety Apparel and Headwear,' or equivalent revisions, except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section. A person designated by the employer to be responsible for worker safety shall make the selection of the appropriate class of garment." - "When uniformed law enforcement personnel are used to direct traffic, to investigate crashes, or to handle lane closures, obstructed roadways, and disasters, high-visibility safety apparel as described in this Section shall be worn by the law enforcement personnel." - "Except as provided in Paragraph 6 of this Section, firefighters or other emergency responders working within the right-of-way shall wear high-visibility safety apparel as described in this Section." Guidance (recommended): - For flagger wear during nighttime activity, high-visibility safety apparel meeting the Performance Class 3 requirements of ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 (or equivalent revision), and labeled as meeting the ANSI 107-2015 standard performance for Class 3 risk exposure, should be worn. - All on-scene responders and news media personnel at traffic incidents should constantly be aware of their visibility to oncoming traffic and wear high-visibility apparel. Options (permitted): - Emergency and incident responders and law enforcement personnel within the TTC zone may wear high-visibility safety apparel that meets the performance requirements of ANSI/ISEA 207-2006 ("American National Standard for High-Visibility Public Safety Vests"), or equivalent revisions, and labeled as ANSI 207-2006, in lieu of ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 apparel. Visual evidence: [Image 5] shows the Part 6 table of contents listing Section 6C.05 "High-Visibility Safety Apparel" within Chapter 6C, Pedestrian and Worker Safety. [Image 6] shows the full text of Section 6C.05, including the Standard, Option, and Guidance paragraphs on apparel requirements. The remaining images ([Image 1], [Image 2], [Image 3], [Image 4], [Image 7], [Image 8]) depict signs, symbols, and mounting methods and do not bear directly on apparel requirements. Citations: - Section 6C.05 Standard §1 (p.782) - Section 6C.05 Standard §3 (p.782) - Section 6C.05 Standard §5 (p.782) - Section 6C.05 Option §4 (p.782) - Section 6C.05 Guidance §7 (p.783) - Section 6O.01 Guidance §7 (p.854) - Page 22 - Page 823
gold_answer: Workers, including emergency responders, within the right-of-way and TTC zone must wear ANSI/ISEA 107-2015 Performance Class 2 or 3 apparel, or an equivalent revision, subject to specified responder exceptions. The employer's designated safety person selects the appropriate class.
